tests_notes: Empty input, first-occurrence order, input not mutated, case-sensitive default, ignore_case keeps the first spelling; workload: 3000 words, 900 distinct.

A.strategy: Track seen keys in a set
A.rationale: The membership test on the `seen` list is O(n), so the loop is O(n·k). A set makes each test O(1); the result list and the order it is built in are unchanged.

B.rationale: Dicts keep insertion order and hash their keys. dict.fromkeys dedupes in C; with ignore_case, setdefault keeps the first spelling per lower-cased key. Same output, linear time.

C.rationale: Conservative micro-optimization: hoists the two attribute lookups out of the loop. Behaviour is unchanged; the list scan stays, so any gain is small.

notes: Happy path: two real wins (set, dict) and a timid micro-optimization that the bench cannot tell apart from the original.
